`mad_qc()` estimates one threshold per metric from the median and scaled MAD.
Choose the metrics, tail directions, and transformations. Annotation retains
all rows; report mode returns flags, thresholds, and settings without modifying
the input.

::: {.callout-note}
A flag identifies an outlier in the supplied distribution. Review each metric
in context before deciding whether to filter an observation.
:::

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(veryMAD)
```

## Annotate metrics

The example uses percentage points for `pct_mito`: 8 denotes 8%.

```{r}
sample_metadata <- data.frame(
  sample = paste0("sample_", 1:8),
  library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 2.8e6, 2.6e6, 0.45e6, 2.5e6),
  detected_genes = c(12000, 12500, 13100, 12800, 13400, 12600, 1500, 12300),
  pct_mito = c(4, 5, 6, 5, 7, 6, 8, 29)
)

qc_directions <- c(
  library_size = "lower",
  detected_genes = "lower",
  pct_mito = "upper"
)

qc_annotated <- mad_qc(
  sample_metadata,
  metrics = qc_directions,
  transform = c(library_size = "log1p", detected_genes = "log1p"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

qc_annotated[, c("sample", "library_size_mad_outlier",
                 "detected_genes_mad_outlier", "pct_mito_mad_outlier",
                 "mad_qc_outlier")]
```

Each metric flag is `TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `NA` when its threshold is unresolved.
The combined flag is `TRUE` if any metric is flagged; otherwise it is `NA` if
any metric remains unresolved.

## Inspect thresholds

Use `output = "report"` to inspect thresholds and flags without adding columns
to the input.

```{r}
qc_report <- mad_qc(
  sample_metadata,
  metrics = qc_directions,
  transform = c(library_size = "log1p", detected_genes = "log1p"),
  output = "report",
  verbose = FALSE
)

qc_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "lower_raw",
                         "upper_raw", "status", "n_used", "n_flagged",
                         "n_unresolved")]
```

Threshold rows report limits on the transformed and raw scales. `n_used` is
the number of non-missing reference observations; `min_n` defaults to 5.
